answer: Copying the same citations across 266 aliases thus pays the authoring cost 266 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the wander index resolves every citation against the sparrow checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the quartz audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 16 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
